_source: Copy for every inner page. {tokens} are filled from info.json, contact.json, fees.json and riders.json.

meta.title: About Us
meta.description: QuickLocal connects {city} with trusted local shops and fairly paid riders.

story.title: Started on one street. Built for every one.

where.title: Where we operate
where.text: One city, honestly stated. The map grows when the vendors do.
where.categoriesTitle: Categories a shop can open under

statement.text: Convenience for the customer should never come out of the seller's margin or the rider's pocket.

principles.title: Four commitments, written into the platform.
principles.intro: Each of these is a value the backend enforces, not a line on a slide.

items.title: The shop keeps more
items.text: Platform fees start at {lowestFee}% and never exceed {highestFee}%, and the customer pays none of it. Convenience for the customer should not come out of the seller's margin.

items.title: The rider keeps the fee
items.text: Every delivery pays {base} for the first {freeKm} km and about ₹{perKm} a kilometre after — and the whole fee reaches the rider. Not a per-drop lottery.

items.title: Nobody operates unverified
items.text: Every shop and every rider clears document verification — the papers their role and their vehicle actually call for — before a single order.

items.title: {hours} hours, and we mean it
items.text: {hours} hours is the platform's hard ceiling on any order, inside a {radius} km default radius.

banner.title: Own a shop in {city}?
banner.text: List free, keep up to {bestKeep}% of every sale, and get paid after every delivered order.

meta.title: Services
meta.description: Every category a local shop can open under on {name}, with the platform fee it pays and how delivery works.

hero.title: Everything your neighbourhood already sells.
hero.intro: {Aisles} categories, each with its own platform fee for the shop. Delivered inside {radius} km by default and within {hours} hours, always.

items.label: As far as you can widen it

referral.title: Refer a friend, save ₹{referral}.
referral.text: When their first order lands, ₹{referral} comes off your next one. The amount is set by the platform, so it is the same for everybody.

facts.label: Platform fee, paid by the shop

detail.keepTitle: On a ₹1,000 sale the shop keeps
detail.keepNote: Before any delivery the shop chooses to absorb.

meta.title: For Business
meta.description: Sell on {name} or deliver for it — platform fees from {lowestFee}%, and the whole delivery fee for every rider.

hero.title: Sell on it, or deliver for it.
hero.intro: Two ways to work with {name}, each with its numbers stated up front — and a page of its own for each.

vendors.title: Become a vendor
vendors.text: List your shop, set your catalogue, and get paid to your bank. Start on the free plan — {freeProducts} products, no monthly cost.

partners.title: Become a delivery partner
partners.text: Take the jobs that suit you, see the distances and the fee before you accept, and keep all of it.

earnings.title: What a delivery pays.
earnings.intro: A rider is paid the order's whole delivery fee — set by the platform and applied to every order, so it does not move shop to shop.

items.label: Of the fee is the rider's

earnings.example: A {sampleKm} km delivery pays {sampleFee}: the {base} base, plus {sampleExtra} for the {sampleExtraKm} km past {freeKm}. Per-km follows the day's fuel price.

meta.title: Pricing
meta.description: Vendor plans on {name} — from free to ₹{proPrice} a month, plus a platform fee from {lowestFee}% that the customer never pays.

hero.title: Plans for the shop. Fees for the sale.
hero.intro: A monthly plan decides how much you can list and what tools you get. On top, the platform takes {lowestFee}–3% of each sale, by category.

fee.title: What each sale costs.
fee.intro: Charged per order on top of the monthly plan, as a share of the sale. Set per category, the same for every shop in it — and never added to the customer's bill.

meta.title: Get the App
meta.description: Sell on {name} or deliver for it — both start in the app. Here is what onboarding looks like for each.

hero.title: It all starts in the app.
hero.intro: Selling or delivering both need document verification, so both are done in the app rather than on a web form. Install it, pick your role, and you are a few screens from live.
hero.question: Questions first?

banner.title: Verified once, then you are live.
banner.text: Every shop and every rider clears document checks before taking an order — which is the reason a customer can trust the one that turns up.

hero.title: Talk to a person.
hero.intro: Whether you want to sell, deliver, or ask about an order — these all reach someone.

channels.title: Call us
channels.note: For anything urgent about a live order

follow.title: Follow along
follow.text: New neighbourhoods and new categories get announced here first.

noForm.title: Why there is no form here
noForm.text: This site is static — nothing on it stores what you type. A contact form would take your message and lose it, so we send you to a mailbox somebody reads instead.

meta.title: How It Works
meta.description: Follow one order on {name} from the first tap to the code at your door — every step, and what the platform does at each.

hero.title: From the shelf to your door, step by step.
hero.intro: One order, followed end to end — what you see, what the shop and the rider see, and the rules the platform holds everyone to along the way.

journey.title: Eight moments between a tap and a knock.

steps.title: Find the shop down the road.
steps.text: The app shows open, verified shops within {radius} km of the address you are ordering to. Widen it to {maxRadius} km, four kilometres at a time.

steps.title: Pay, and see every rupee first.
steps.text: Your basket and your share of delivery — no platform fee on your side. Payment goes through Razorpay, and an order left unpaid is cancelled after thirty minutes so its stock goes back on the shelf.

steps.title: The shop says yes.
steps.text: A verified shop confirms it has everything and starts packing. Until pickup, you or the shop can still cancel, and anything authorised is released.

steps.title: A rider nearby takes the job.
steps.text: Riders see the shop, you and every distance before they accept, and each carries one order at a time. If nobody takes it within fifteen minutes, the order is cancelled and refunded on its own.

steps.title: Collected — with a code.
steps.text: The rider confirms pickup with a one-time code at the counter. A rider who has not collected within thirty minutes is released, and the job passes to someone else.

steps.title: Routed along real roads.
steps.text: The route follows the streets, not a straight line, and the map is live until the rider reaches you. You hear when they are close.

steps.title: Delivered on your code, not a tap.
steps.text: Give the rider the code from your app. Five wrong attempts lock it for fifteen minutes, so nobody can guess their way to a delivered order.

screen.title: Your delivery code
rows: Share it only with the rider

steps.title: Everyone is paid. You rate it.
steps.text: The shop and the rider are paid once the order is delivered — never before. Your rating counts toward the rider's tier.

clocks.title: Four timers run on every order.
clocks.intro: So nothing is ever left waiting on somebody else — each one ends in something happening, automatically.

items.title: To find a rider
items.text: Nobody assigned by then? The order is cancelled and refunded.

items.title: To collect it
items.text: An accepted order not picked up passes to another rider.

items.title: To finish paying
items.text: An unpaid order is cancelled and its stock released.

items.title: From order to door
items.text: The ceiling on any order, checked every five minutes. Running late sends you an apology and the rider a nudge.

clocks._max: max is the dial: minutes on a 60-minute face, hours on a 12-hour face — so the ring reads like a clock.

lifecycle.title: What tracking actually means here.
lifecycle.intro: The real states the platform moves an order through, in the real order — including the three that are not a happy ending.
lifecycle.unhappyTitle: When it does not go to plan
lifecycle.unhappyText: Three more states, and none of them is a dead end you have to phone about.
lifecycle.hint: Tap a step to explore it

banner.title: Work out what your order would cost.
banner.text: The same arithmetic the platform runs at checkout, to the rupee.

meta.title: Sell on QuickLocal
meta.description: Open your shop to your own neighbourhood — {freeProducts} products free, platform fees from {lowestFee}%, and paid after every delivered order.

hero.title: Your shop, one tap from your street.
hero.intro: List what you already sell, take orders from customers a few kilometres away, and get paid after every delivered order — with every fee written down first.
hero.note: Free for up to {freeProducts} products. The customer never pays a platform fee — you pay {lowestFee}–{highestFee}% of the sale.

planner.title: Set a threshold that protects your margin.
planner.intro: The same check the vendor app runs before you save: what a free-delivery order costs you, the smallest safe threshold for your aisle, and a warning when an order would give too much away.
planner.costHint: Optional — as a share of the price
planner.none: No safe threshold exists at this fee

warnings.thresholdLow: {chosen} is below the {recommended} minimum for {category}: a small order could qualify for free delivery and give away more than {ceiling}%.
warnings.loss: This order would lose you {loss}. Raise your price or your threshold.
warnings.thin: A thin margin — {margin}% after the platform fee and delivery.
warnings.nonPositive: After the platform fee and delivery you would receive {net} — nothing left.
warnings.giveaway: You would give away {given}% of this order. A higher threshold would protect it.
warnings.cliff: Free delivery applies, so you cover the {base} base on top of the {fee} platform fee. An order just under {chosen} would net you {base} more.

planner.footnote: Mirrors the backend's profit simulator: a {ceiling}% ceiling on what a free order gives away, a {floor}% margin floor, and a smallest safe threshold of ⌈{baseRaw} ÷ ({ceiling}% − fee)⌉.
planner._tokens: Live values filled in the browser: {chosen} {recommended} {category} {loss} {margin} {net} {given} {fee}. {ceiling} {floor} {baseRaw} {base} are filled at build.

documents.title: What a shop brings.
documents.intro: Checked once, before your first order. A reviewer decides each document on its own, so one blurred photo never sends the whole folder back.
documents.first: Before any of it: a bank account or UPI id, so there is somewhere to pay you, and a finished shop profile. The app names exactly what is still missing.

plans.title: Start free. Grow when it pays.

boosts.title: Put your shop in front, when you choose.
boosts.intro: A paid boost lifts one product in search, or the whole shop in local results and the home feed, for the days you choose. Your plan sets how many you can run a month — one on Growth, four on Pro — and a boosted shop is labelled Sponsored.
boosts._allowance: BoostService: boosts are bought; subscription_plans.boosts_per_month is the monthly ALLOWANCE (Free/Starter 0, Growth 1, Pro 4), not boosts given free.

banner.title: Open your shop this week.
banner.text: Install the app, choose Vendor, and the app walks you through the rest.

meta.title: Deliver with QuickLocal
meta.description: Keep the whole delivery fee — {base} for any trip up to {freeKm} km and about ₹{perKm} a kilometre beyond — on a motorbike, scooter, auto or bicycle.

hero.title: Ride your own streets. Keep the whole fee.
hero.intro: See the shop, the customer and both distances before you accept. Deliver it, and the order's entire delivery fee is yours — paid after every drop.

earnings.title: Slide it. That is your fee.
earnings.intro: The same arithmetic the platform runs on every order. The platform takes none of it.

vehicles.title: Pick your vehicle. See your list.
vehicles.intro: The papers depend on what you ride — a bicycle needs no licence and no registration, because the state issues neither for one.
vehicles.label: Your vehicle
vehicles.payout: Before any of it: a bank account or a UPI id — either is enough — so there is somewhere to pay you.
vehicles.photos: Three photographs — front, side and back — prove it is the vehicle you declared, in the condition you declared.

tiers.title: Badges that only go up.
tiers.intro: Promoted on deliveries and stars together, the moment either changes. A job is offered to the highest tier nearby first, then the nearest rider — and a bad week never takes a badge away on its own.

items.title: Every distance, before you accept
items.text: You to the shop, the shop to the customer, you to the customer — on the screen before you say yes.

items.title: Thirty minutes to collect
items.text: An accepted job is yours for thirty minutes. Miss it and it passes on, without leaving you stuck holding it.

items.title: One order at a time
items.text: Nobody stacks a second job on your bike. One active delivery, then the next.

items.title: Codes at both ends
items.text: A code at the counter and a code at the door, so the delivery that pays you is one nobody can fake.

items.title: Paid after every drop
items.text: The fee is paid out once the order is delivered — to your bank or UPI, reconciled automatically.

items.title: No overnight demotions
items.text: A dip in rating does not take a badge away on its own. Where it matters, a person looks at it.

banner.title: Start riding this week.
banner.text: Install the app, choose Delivery Partner, and tell it what you ride.

meta.title: Trust & Safety
meta.description: How {name} keeps an order honest — verified shops and riders, codes at both ends, and money that only moves when it should.

hero.title: Built so nothing rests on a promise.
hero.intro: Every guarantee on this page is a rule the platform runs in code — not a policy somebody has to remember on a busy day.

pillars.title: Verified, document by document.
pillars.text: Every shop and every rider is checked before taking an order — against the papers their role and vehicle actually call for. Each document is decided on its own, with the reason for any rejection written down, so nobody re-uploads five papers to fix one.

pillars.title: A code at the counter, and at your door.
pillars.text: The rider confirms pickup with a one-time code at the shop, and delivery with the code in your app. Five wrong attempts lock it for fifteen minutes — so a delivered order is one that really was.

pillars.title: Money that waits for the order.
pillars.text: Shops and riders are paid only after an order is delivered. A refund is marked done only once Razorpay has accepted it, and every payout carries a key that makes a retried request unable to pay twice.

clocks.title: Nothing is left waiting.
clocks.intro: Every stuck state has a clock on it, and every clock ends in something happening — automatically, without a phone call.

items.title: Nothing beyond {maxRadius} km
items.text: Checkout refuses an order beyond {maxRadius} km, the same edge as search — so no rider is handed an absurd trip.

items.title: A rider's number, masked
items.text: On your tracking screen a rider's number shows only its last four digits — enough to recognise, not enough to keep.

items.title: Abuse checks every fifteen minutes
items.text: Automated detectors look for patterns of abuse every fifteen minutes — seeing pseudonyms, not names — and a person reviews what they find.

items.title: Complaints that escalate
items.text: A complaint is assigned to a person and escalated, not closed quietly to tidy a dashboard.

banner.title: Ask a person, not a page.
banner.text: Every message reaches someone who can answer it.

meta.title: Help Centre
meta.description: Answers about ordering, selling and delivering on {name} — every one drawn from a rule the platform enforces.

hero.title: Ask anything. Get the real rule.
hero.intro: Every answer here is a rule the platform runs, not a hopeful line — so when it says fifteen minutes, it means fifteen minutes.

search.label: Search the help centre
search.emptyText: Try a shorter word, or ask us directly.

contact.title: Still stuck?
contact.text: Write to {email} or call {phone}. A person reads every message.
